findings.title: Incomplete intake records delay assignment
findings.summary: Requests missing an owner, due date, or source reference require manual follow-up before work can begin.
evidence: 12 of 40 sampled requests were missing at least one required intake field.
Eight of those requests waited more than one business day for clarification.
findings.recommended_action: Validate the required intake fields before a request enters the assignment queue.

findings.title: Escalations use inconsistent categories
findings.summary: Similar escalation reasons are recorded under several labels, which makes routing and trend review less reliable.
evidence: Five labels were used for the same access-related escalation pattern.
Two cases were routed to the wrong queue before being reassigned.
findings.recommended_action: Replace overlapping escalation labels with one short controlled list and an explicit fallback category.

findings.title: Missing source notes increase rework
findings.summary: Reviewers repeat discovery work when a request states a conclusion without linking the note, record, or observation that supports it.
evidence: Nine sampled requests required a second source lookup.
The repeated lookup added an estimated 95 minutes across the sample.
findings.recommended_action: Require one source label and link for every submitted finding before review begins.
